test_title: PYST 42: SSC CPO - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on 11 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: 8 men and 12 women finish a job in 4 days. While 6 men and 14 women in 5 days. In how many days will 20 women finish the job?
solution:
**Given:**

8 men and 12 women finish a job in 4 days

6 men and 14 women in 5 days

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let 1 man's and 1 woman's 1-day work be x and y respectively

⇒ Then, 8x + 12y = (1)/(4) --------(1)

⇒ 6x + 14y = (1)/(5) --------(2)

⇒ Multiplying equation 1 by 6 and equation 2 by 8 we get,

⇒ 48x + 72y = (3)/(2) --------(3)

⇒ 48x + 112y = (8)/(5) --------(4)

⇒ Subtracting equation 3 from 4 we get,

⇒ 40y = (1)/(10)

⇒ y = (1)/(400)

⇒ Thus 1 woman can finish it in 400 days

⇒ So time taken by 20 women to finish the work = (400)/(20) = 20 days

**Therefore, 20 women can finish the job in 20 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Concept used:**

• M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

• Total work done = Efficiency × Total number of days

**Calculation: **

⇒ (8M + 12W) × 4 = (6M + 14W) × 5

⇒ 32M + 48W = 30M + 70W

⇒ 2M = 22W

⇒ (M)/(W) = (11)/(1) [ efficiency of M : W = 11 : 1 ]

So, the total work done is,

⇒ [ (8 × 11) + (12 × 1) ] × 4

⇒ [ 88 + 12 ] × 4

⇒ 400

So, 20 women do this work in (400)/(20) = 20 days
